title: Last slice. Part 1
note: Silent. Frame 1 fully composed, no fade, ONE strip (hook, 0-3.0, y=345, guest-check slip). Night diner counter, neon OPEN in the window, clock 11:41 PM. Two large faces: his phone lit mid-swipe (generic profile-card glow, no UI; thumb flicks 0.2-1.4), her phone lit too in one hand (pink case), and in her other hand the biggest, brightest object: a white napkin reading 'that's my slice.' in cranberry crayon. Behind them the glowing pie case with ONE slice of pumpkin pie and a LAST SLICE clip sign, plus a crayon cup (pumpkin, cranberry stubs) and the chrome napkin dispenser. Season opener: no take 1, no rewind. Own payoff before the cliff: the plate push-back standoff, the cream dollop landing on his ear and their shared laugh (13.3), then both phones under upside-down mugs (15.3, 15.9). Cliff: she writes 'split it? / who gets first bite?' on a new napkin; his phone buzzes under the mug and he ignores it (22.0-22.4); slice wipe to the vote board by 23.7 s. Whenever a napkin carries a line it is a WHOLE-FRAME insert (napkin ~800 px wide, centred around y=760, Patrick Hand 700 crayon drawn in; hers lowercase cranberry, his ALL CAPS pumpkin; no parentheses). Text only between y=270 and y=1250. No NoSwipe mention. No real diner or place names. She is warm and equal: the only jokes are his pushes, his ear and his flush. Waitress is silent. Strips are first person. NOTE: never use the word 'tip' (reads as gratuity at a diner); the stake is 'first bite'. ROUND 2: waitress adult behind counter; phones-in-mugs is a counter close-up (phones face-down, mug drops, light pool); best bite label drawn by 18.2; split-it napkin clean by 20.6; mug-buzz close-up 22.0-23.2 (wipe/vote/end +0.5 s); napkin handoff + shared laugh 13.3-14.3.

choices.why: Both about him. A is the polite lie, B the honest bold answer. B is the planned winner. Part 2 plays A first and fails on him (his stomach growls so loud the mugs rattle, the waitress deadpans a second fork), slice wipe reverses as the rewind, then B carries on.

strips.text: the stranger on the next stool wants my last slice of pie.
she caught me swiping. now we both want the last slice.
thanksgiving eve. we both ordered the last slice.
I pushed it over. she pushed it back.
we did this for a while.
she put her phone in a mug.
my mug buzzed. I let it.
she asked who gets first bite. what do I write?
